THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING BEEN CAME UP FOR HEARING ON 04.03.2026, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 W,P(C) No.3424 of 2024  . .3..
 2026:KER:19566  J U D G M E N T Dated this the 4th day of March, 2026 Petitioner surrendered landed property having an extent of 47.52 cents in Nattakam Village, Kottayam, for the project 'Kottayam Development Corridor'.
The surrender was free of cost, on condition that the Government will permit conversion of the remaining paddy land as dry land for the construction of building.
Ext.P4 is the Government Order in this regard.
However, no permission as contemplated in Ext.P4 was granted.
Besides, Ext.P6 Order was passed to the effect that the changing the character of the remaining property would violate the provisions of the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the value of the land has to be reckoned as on the date of . .4..
2026:KER:19566 the notification; and not as on the date of surrender.
Notification is yet to be issued, and therefore the present market rate is liable to be reckoned, is the argument advanced.

Learned counsel would also submit that the issue involved in this Writ Petition is covered by a judgment of this Court dated 17.10.2025 in W.P.(C)No.9775/2025, as also, another judgment which is produced in the Writ Petition, at Ext.P7.
3.
Learned Government Pleader would also agree that the issue stands covered by the afore-referred judgments.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader, this Court finds that the petitioner is entitled to compensation in terms of the market value prevailing as on the date of notification, as held in Ext.P7 judgment.

Learned Government Pleader would submit that the Special Tahsildar (Land Acquisition), Kottayam, is the person who has to pass an Award in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land .

.5..
2026:KER:19566 Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act, 2013,. In the circumstances,
the Special Tahsildar (Land Acquisition), Kottayam, is suo moto impleaded as the additional 7th respondent.

5. The additionally impleaded 7th respondent will, therefore, stand directed to grant petitioner all the benefits afforded in Ext.P7 judgment, as also, in W.P.(C)No.26234/2023, and to pass an Award,
as directed in the latter judgment, within a period of four months from the date of production of a copy of this judgment.
There will be a further direction to disburse the compensation amount in terms of the Award within a further period of two months from the date of passing the Award.
The right of the petitioner to challenge the Award, in case they are not satisfied of the same, stands reserved.

Since the acquisition took place in the year 2011 and the petitioner has been deprived of his valuable property from that point of time onwards, the timeline stipulated above will be strictly adhered to.
The Writ Petition (Civil) will stand disposed of as above.

Sd/-
C. JAYACHANDRAN JUDGE TR . .7..
